sanskrit: maṇḍalāvartamārgeṣu gadāviharaṇeṣu ca nirviśeṣam abhūd yuddhaṃ tayoḥ puruṣasiṃhayoḥ
english: In the wheeling, circling courses and in the play of their maces, the combat of those two lions among men was beyond all distinction.

sanskrit: tāḍitā bhīmasenena śalyasya mahatī gadā sāgnijvālā mahāraudrā gadācūrṇam aśīryata
english: Struck by Bhīmasena, Śalya's great mace, blazing with flame and terrible to behold, was shattered into mace-dust.

sanskrit: tathaiva bhīmasenasya dviṣatābhihatā gadā varṣāpradoṣe khadyotair vṛto vṛkṣa ivābabhau
english: In like manner Bhīmasena's mace, smitten by his foe, gleamed like a tree thronged with fireflies in the early dusk of the rainy season.

sanskrit: gadā kṣiptā tu samare madrarājena bhārata vyoma saṃdīpayānā sā sasṛje pāvakaṃ bahu
english: The mace hurled in battle by the king of the Madras, O Bhārata, kindling the sky, scattered fire in abundance.

sanskrit: tathaiva bhīmasenena dviṣate preṣitā gadā tāpayām āsa tat sainyaṃ maholkā patatī yathā
english: So too the mace sped by Bhīmasena against his foe scorched that host like a great meteor falling.

sanskrit: te caivobhe gade śreṣṭhe samāsādya parasparam śvasantyau nāgakanyeva sasṛjāte vibhāvasum
english: And those two surpassing maces, meeting each other, hissing like serpent-maidens, gave forth fire.

sanskrit: nakhair iva mahāvyāghrau dantair iva mahāgajau tau viceratur āsādya gadābhyāṃ ca parasparam
english: Like two great tigers with their claws, like two great elephants with their tusks, those two ranged about, closing upon each other with their maces.

sanskrit: tato gadāgrābhihatau kṣaṇena rudhirokṣitau dadṛśāte mahātmānau puṣpitāv iva kiṃśukau
english: Then, struck by the heads of the maces and in a moment drenched with blood, those two great-souled warriors appeared like a pair of kiṃśuka trees in flower.

sanskrit: śuśruve dikṣu sarvāsu tayoḥ puruṣasiṃhayoḥ gadābhighātasaṃhrādaḥ śakrāśanir ivopamaḥ
english: In every quarter was heard the clash and crash of the mace-blows of those two lions among men, like to the thunderbolt of Indra.

sanskrit: gadayā madrarājena savyadakṣiṇam āhataḥ nākampata tadā bhīmo bhidyamāna ivācalaḥ
english: Struck on left and right by the king of the Madras' mace, Bhīma did not waver then, like a mountain being riven yet unmoved.

sanskrit: tathā bhīmagadāvegais tāḍyamāno mahābalaḥ dhairyān madrādhipas tasthau vajrair girir ivāhataḥ
english: So too, battered by the onsets of Bhīma's mace, the mighty lord of the Madras stood firm by his steadfastness, like a mountain smitten by thunderbolts.

sanskrit: āpetatur mahāvegau samucchritamahāgadau punar antaramārgasthau maṇḍalāni viceratuḥ
english: Rushing on with great speed, their huge maces raised aloft, again, taking the intervening paths, they wheeled about in circles.

sanskrit: athāplutya padāny aṣṭau saṃnipatya gajāv iva sahasā lohadaṇḍābhyām anyonyam abhijaghnatuḥ
english: Then, springing forward eight paces and clashing together like two elephants, of a sudden they smote each other with their iron staves.

sanskrit: tau parasparavegāc ca gadābhyāṃ ca bhṛśāhatau yugapat petatur vīrau kṣitāv indradhvajāv iva
english: And by their mutual onslaught and by their maces sorely battered, the two heroes fell at once to the earth like two banners of Indra.

sanskrit: tato vihvalamānaṃ taṃ niḥśvasantaṃ punaḥ punaḥ śalyam abhyapatat tūrṇaṃ kṛtavarmā mahārathaḥ
english: Then to Śalya, reeling and gasping again and again, Kṛtavarman the great chariot-warrior swiftly came.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā cainaṃ mahārāja gadayābhinipīḍitam viceṣṭantaṃ yathā nāgaṃ mūrchayābhipariplutam
english: And seeing him, O great king, crushed by the mace, writhing like a serpent and overwhelmed by a swoon,

sanskrit: tataḥ sagadam āropya madrāṇām adhipaṃ ratham apovāha raṇāt tūrṇaṃ kṛtavarmā mahārathaḥ
english: then, lifting the lord of the Madras together with his mace onto his chariot, Kṛtavarman the great chariot-warrior swiftly bore him away from the battle.

sanskrit: kṣībavad vihvalo vīro nimeṣāt punar utthitaḥ bhīmo 'pi sumahābāhur gadāpāṇir adṛśyata
english: The hero, reeling as though drunken, rose again within the twinkling of an eye; and mighty-armed Bhīma too was seen, mace in hand.

sanskrit: tato madrādhipaṃ dṛṣṭvā tava putrāḥ parāṅmukham sanāgarathapattyaśvāḥ samakampanta māriṣa
english: Then, seeing the lord of the Madras turned away in flight, your sons, with their elephants, chariots, foot, and horse, trembled, O venerable one.

sanskrit: te pāṇḍavair ardyamānās tāvakā jitakāśibhiḥ bhītā diśo 'nvapadyanta vātanunnā ghanā iva
english: Your men, harried by the victory-flushed Pāṇḍavas, took in fear to the quarters of the sky like clouds driven before the wind.

sanskrit: nirjitya dhārtarāṣṭrāṃs tu pāṇḍaveyā mahārathāḥ vyarocanta raṇe rājan dīpyamānā yaśasvinaḥ
english: Having vanquished the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the great chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas shone resplendent in the battle, O king, blazing and full of glory.

sanskrit: siṃhanādān bhṛśaṃ cakruḥ śaṅkhān dadhmuś ca harṣitāḥ bherīś ca vādayām āsur mṛdaṅgāṃś cānakaiḥ saha
english: Loudly they raised their lion-roars and, in their joy, blew their conches and sounded kettledrums and tabors along with the war-drums.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tad balaṃ sumahad dīrṇaṃ tvadīyaṃ prekṣya vīryavān dadhāraiko raṇe pāṇḍūn vṛṣaseno 'stramāyayā
english: Saṃjaya said: Beholding that vast host of yours broken in flight, valiant Vṛṣasena alone withstood the Pāṇḍavas in battle by the cunning of his weapons.

sanskrit: śarā daśa diśo muktā vṛṣasenena māriṣa vicerus te vinirbhidya naravājirathadvipān
english: The arrows loosed by Vṛṣasena toward the ten quarters ranged abroad, O venerable one, piercing through men, horses, chariots, and elephants.

sanskrit: tasya dīptā mahābāṇā viniśceruḥ sahasraśaḥ bhānor iva mahābāho grīṣmakāle marīcayaḥ
english: His blazing great shafts issued forth by the thousand, O mighty-armed one, like the rays of the sun in the season of summer.

sanskrit: tenārditā mahārāja rathinaḥ sādinas tathā nipetur urvyāṃ sahasā vātanunnā iva drumāḥ
english: Tormented by him, O great king, chariot-warriors and horsemen alike fell suddenly upon the earth like trees uprooted by the wind.

sanskrit: hayaughāṃś ca rathaughāṃś ca gajaughāṃś ca samantataḥ apātayad raṇe rājañ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Floods of horses, floods of chariots, and floods of elephants on every side he brought down in battle, O king, by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tam evaṃ samare vicarantam abhītavat sahitāḥ sarvarājānaḥ parivavruḥ samantataḥ
english: Seeing him thus ranging fearless through the battle, all the kings together hemmed him in on every side.

sanskrit: nākulis tu śatānīko vṛṣasenaṃ samabhyayāt vivyādha cainaṃ daśabhir nārācair marmabhedibhiḥ
english: But Śatānīka, son of Nakula, advanced against Vṛṣasena and pierced him with ten iron shafts that cut to the vitals.

sanskrit: tasya karṇātmajaś cāpaṃ chittvā ketum apātayat taṃ bhrātaraṃ parīpsanto draupadeyāḥ samabhyayuḥ
english: Karṇa's son sundered his bow and felled his banner; and the sons of Draupadī, seeking to protect that brother of theirs, advanced together.

sanskrit: karṇātmajaṃ śaravrātaiś cakruś cādṛśyam añjasā tān nadanto 'bhyadhāvanta droṇaputramukhā rathāḥ
english: With showers of arrows they made Karṇa's son straightway invisible; whereupon the chariot-warriors, with Droṇa's son at their head, ran roaring against them.

sanskrit: chādayanto mahārāja draupadeyān mahārathān śarair nānāvidhais tūrṇaṃ parvatāñ jaladā iva
english: Swiftly veiling the great chariot-warriors, the sons of Draupadī, with arrows of many kinds, O great king, as rain-clouds veil the mountains.

sanskrit: tān pāṇḍavāḥ pratyagṛhṇaṃs tvaritāḥ putragṛddhinaḥ pāñcālāḥ kekayā matsyāḥ sṛñjayāś codyatāyudhāḥ
english: The Pāṇḍavas, eager for their sons, received them in haste—the Pāñcālas, the Kekayas, the Matsyas, and the Sṛñjayas, weapons upraised.

sanskrit: tad yuddham abhavad ghoraṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam tvadīyaiḥ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ devānām iva dānavaiḥ
english: Dreadful, tumultuous, and hair-raising was that battle between your men and the sons of Pāṇḍu, as of the gods with the dānavas.

sanskrit: evam uttamasaṃrambhā yuyudhuḥ kurupāṇḍavāḥ parasparam udīkṣantaḥ parasparakṛtāgasaḥ
english: Thus, with utmost fury, the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas fought, glaring upon one another, each having wronged the other.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ dadṛśire kopād vapūṃṣy amitatejasām yuyutsūnām ivākāśe patatrivarabhoginām
english: In their wrath the forms of those of measureless might were seen, like the bodies of the noblest of winged serpents joined in combat in the sky.

sanskrit: bhīmakarṇakṛpadroṇadrauṇipārṣatasātyakaiḥ babhāse sa raṇoddeśaḥ kālasūryair ivoditaiḥ
english: With Bhīma, Karṇa, Kṛpa, Droṇa, Droṇa's son, the son of Pṛṣata, and Sātyaki, that field of battle shone as with risen suns of doom.

sanskrit: tadāsīt tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ nighnatām itaretaram mahābalānāṃ balibhir dānavānāṃ yathā suraiḥ
english: Then was waged a tumultuous battle of mighty ones smiting one another, as of the strong gods with the dānavas.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhirānīkam uddhūtārṇavanisvanam tvadīyam avadhīt sainyaṃ saṃpradrutamahāratham
english: Then the host of Yudhiṣṭhira, roaring like an upheaved ocean, smote down your army, whose great chariot-warriors had taken to flight.

sanskrit: tat prabhagnaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā śatrubhir bhṛśam arditam alaṃ drutena vaḥ śūrā iti droṇo 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Seeing that host broken and sorely afflicted by the foe, Droṇa cried out, "Enough of your flight, O heroes!"

sanskrit: tataḥ śoṇahayaḥ kruddhaś caturdanta iva dvipaḥ praviśya pāṇḍavānīkaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram upādravat
english: Then he of the red steeds, enraged, like a four-tusked elephant, entered the host of the Pāṇḍavas and rushed upon Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tam avidhyac chitair bāṇaiḥ kaṅkapatrair yudhiṣṭhiraḥ tasya droṇo dhanuś chittvā taṃ drutaṃ samupādravat
english: Yudhiṣṭhira pierced him with sharp shafts feathered with heron-plumes; but Droṇa, sundering his bow, swiftly bore down upon him.

sanskrit: cakrarakṣaḥ kumāras tu pāñcālānāṃ yaśaskaraḥ dadhāra droṇam āyāntaṃ veleva saritāṃ patim
english: But the prince Kumāra, guardian of the chariot-wheel and bringer of glory to the Pāñcālas, stayed the advancing Droṇa as the shore stays the lord of rivers.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ nivāritaṃ dṛṣṭvā kumāreṇa dvijarṣabham siṃhanādaravo hy āsīt sādhu sādhv iti bhāṣatām
english: Seeing Droṇa, that bull among the twice-born, held back by Kumāra, there arose a lion-roar from those who cried, "Well done! Well done!"

sanskrit: kumāras tu tato droṇaṃ sāyakena mahāhave vivyādhorasi saṃkruddhaḥ siṃhavac cānadan muhuḥ
english: Then Kumāra, in that great fray, in his wrath pierced Droṇa in the breast with a shaft, roaring again and again like a lion.

sanskrit: saṃvārya tu raṇe droṇaḥ kumāraṃ vai mahābalaḥ śarair anekasāhasraiḥ kṛtahasto jitaklamaḥ
english: But the mighty Droṇa, deft of hand and unwearied, having checked Kumāra in the battle with many thousands of arrows,

sanskrit: taṃ śūram āryavratinam astrārthakṛtaniśramam cakrarakṣam apāmṛdnāt kumāraṃ dvijasattamaḥ
english: that best of the twice-born crushed Kumāra—the hero, faithful to noble vows, schooled in the lore of weapons, the guardian of the wheel.

sanskrit: sa madhyaṃ prāpya senāyāḥ sarvāḥ paricaran diśaḥ tava sainyasya goptāsīd bhāradvājo ratharṣabhaḥ
english: Reaching the midst of the army and ranging through all the quarters, Bhāradvāja, that bull among chariot-warriors, became the protector of your host.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ dvādaśabhir viṃśatyā cottamaujasam nakulaṃ pañcabhir viddhvā sahadevaṃ ca saptabhiḥ
english: Piercing Śikhaṇḍin with twelve shafts, Uttamaujas with twenty, Nakula with five, and Sahadeva with seven,

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ dvādaśabhir draupadeyāṃs tribhis tribhiḥ sātyakiṃ pañcabhir viddhvā matsyaṃ ca daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira with twelve, the sons of Draupadī with three apiece, Sātyaki with five, and the Matsya king with ten arrows—

sanskrit: vyakṣobhayad raṇe yodhān yathāmukhyān abhidravan abhyavartata saṃprepsuḥ kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: he threw the foremost warriors into confusion in the battle, charging upon them; and he pressed forward, seeking to seize Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: yugaṃdharas tato rājan bhāradvājaṃ mahāratham vārayām āsa saṃkruddhaṃ vātoddhūtam ivārṇavam
english: Then, O king, Yugaṃdhara held back Bhāradvāja, that great chariot-warrior in his wrath, as a shore holds back the wind-tossed ocean.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ sa viddhvā tu śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ yugaṃdharaṃ ca bhallena rathanīḍād apāharat
english: But he, piercing Yudhiṣṭhira with arrows of well-bent joints, with a broad-headed shaft swept Yugaṃdhara from the platform of his chariot.

sanskrit: tato virāṭadrupadau kekayāḥ sātyakiḥ śibiḥ vyāghradattaś ca pāñcālyaḥ siṃhasenaś ca vīryavān
english: Then Virāṭa and Drupada, the Kekayas, Sātyaki, Śibi, Vyāghradatta the Pāñcāla, and the valiant Siṃhasena,

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavaḥ parīpsanto yudhiṣṭhiram āvavrus tasya panthānaṃ kirantaḥ sāyakān bahūn
english: these and many others, seeking to protect Yudhiṣṭhira, barred his path, pouring forth many arrows.

sanskrit: vyāghradattaś ca pāñcālyo droṇaṃ vivyādha mārgaṇaiḥ pañcāśadbhiḥ śitai rājaṃs tata uccukruśur janāḥ
english: And Vyāghradatta the Pāñcāla pierced Droṇa with fifty sharp arrows, O king; whereat the people raised a great shout.

sanskrit: tvaritaṃ siṃhasenas tu droṇaṃ viddhvā mahāratham prāhasat sahasā hṛṣṭas trāsayan vai yatavratam
english: And Siṃhasena, swiftly piercing Droṇa, that great chariot-warrior, laughed aloud of a sudden in his joy, seeking to daunt that man of steadfast vows.

sanskrit: tato visphārya nayane dhanurjyām avamṛjya ca talaśabdaṃ mahat kṛtvā droṇas taṃ samupādravat
english: Then, his eyes wide with rage, drawing back the bowstring and making a great clap with his palm, Droṇa bore down upon him.

sanskrit: tatas tu siṃhasenasya śiraḥ kāyāt sakuṇḍalam vyāghradattasya cākramya bhallābhyām aharad balī
english: Then the mighty one, closing in, with two broad-headed shafts struck off from their bodies the heads of Siṃhasena and of Vyāghradatta, earrings and all.

sanskrit: tān pramṛdya śaravrātaiḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathān yudhiṣṭhirasamabhyāśe tasthau mṛtyur ivāntakaḥ
english: Having crushed those great chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas with showers of arrows, he stood close by Yudhiṣṭhira like Death the ender.

sanskrit: tato 'bhavan mahāśabdo rājan yaudhiṣṭhire bale hṛto rājeti yodhānāṃ samīpasthe yatavrate
english: Then there arose a great clamor, O king, in the host of Yudhiṣṭhira—"The king is taken!"—from the warriors, as the steadfast-vowed one drew near.

sanskrit: abruvan sainikās tatra dṛṣṭvā droṇasya vikramam adya rājā dhārtarāṣṭraḥ kṛtārtho vai bhaviṣyati āgamiṣyati no nūnaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya saṃyuge
english: Beholding Droṇa's prowess, the soldiers there said, "Today shall the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra surely have his desire; surely he will come to us in the battle of the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra."

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃjalpatāṃ teṣāṃ tāvakānāṃ mahārathaḥ āyāj javena kaunteyo rathaghoṣeṇa nādayan
english: While your men were thus talking together, the great chariot-warrior, the son of Kuntī, came on at speed, making all resound with the thunder of his car.

sanskrit: śoṇitodāṃ rathāvartāṃ kṛtvā viśasane nadīm śūrāsthicayasaṃkīrṇāṃ pretakūlāpahāriṇīm
english: On the field of slaughter he made a river whose waters were blood and whose eddies were chariots, strewn with heaps of heroes' bones, sweeping away the corpses on its banks;

sanskrit: tāṃ śaraughamahāphenāṃ prāsamatsyasamākulām nadīm uttīrya vegena kurūn vidrāvya pāṇḍavaḥ
english: and crossing in haste that river, whose great foam was the floods of arrows and which teemed with javelins for fishes, the Pāṇḍava put the Kurus to flight.

sanskrit: tataḥ kirīṭī sahasā droṇānīkam upādravat chādayann iṣujālena mahatā mohayann iva
english: Then the Diademed one suddenly fell upon Droṇa's host, veiling it with a vast net of arrows as though to bewilder it.

sanskrit: śīghram abhyasyato bāṇān saṃdadhānasya cāniśam nāntaraṃ dadṛśe kaś cit kaunteyasya yaśasvinaḥ
english: As he swiftly loosed his shafts and ceaselessly fitted them anew, no one could mark any interval in the work of the glorious son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: na diśo nāntarikṣaṃ ca na dyaur naiva ca medinī adṛśyata mahārāja bāṇabhūtam ivābhavat
english: Neither the quarters, nor the mid-air, nor the heavens, nor the earth could be seen, O great king; all was become, as it were, one mass of arrows.

sanskrit: nādṛśyata tadā rājaṃs tatra kiṃ cana saṃyuge bāṇāndhakāre mahati kṛte gāṇḍīvadhanvanā
english: Nothing whatsoever could then be seen there in the battle, O king, so great a darkness of arrows had the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva made.

sanskrit: sūrye cāstam anuprāpte rajasā cābhisaṃvṛte nājñāyata tadā śatrur na suhṛn na ca kiṃ cana
english: And as the sun reached its setting and all was wrapped in dust, neither foe nor friend nor anything at all could then be known.

sanskrit: tato 'vahāraṃ cakrus te droṇaduryodhanādayaḥ tān viditvā bhṛśaṃ trastān ayuddhamanasaḥ parān
english: Then Droṇa, Duryodhana, and the rest drew off their forces; and the Pāṇḍava, perceiving the foe sorely affrighted and with no heart for fighting,

sanskrit: svāny anīkāni bībhatsuḥ śanakair avahārayat tato 'bhituṣṭuvuḥ pārthaṃ prahṛṣṭāḥ pāṇḍusṛñjayāḥ pāñcālāś ca manojñābhir vāgbhiḥ sūryam ivarṣayaḥ
english: Bībhatsu gently withdrew his own troops; whereupon the Pāṇḍus, the Sṛñjayas, and the Pāñcālas, rejoicing, extolled Pārtha with pleasing words, as the seers extol the sun.

sanskrit: evaṃ svaśibiraṃ prāyāj jitvā śatrūn dhanaṃjayaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sarvasainyānāṃ mudito vai sakeśavaḥ
english: Thus, having conquered the foe, Dhanaṃjaya, glad of heart and with Keśava beside him, made his way to his own camp behind all the host.

sanskrit: masāragalvarkasuvarṇarūpyair; vajrapravālasphaṭikaiś ca mukhyaiḥ citre rathe pāṇḍusuto babhāse; nakṣatracitre viyatīva candraḥ
english: On his car bright with sapphire, agate, gold, and silver, and with choice diamonds, coral, and crystal, the son of Pāṇḍu shone like the moon in a sky aglitter with stars.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca te sene śibiraṃ gatvā nyaviśetāṃ viśāṃ pate yathābhāgaṃ yathānyāyaṃ yathāgulmaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Those two armies, having gone to their camps, settled down, O lord of peoples, each in its portion, in due order, and by its companies throughout.

sanskrit: kṛtvāvahāraṃ sainyānāṃ droṇaḥ paramadurmanāḥ duryodhanam abhiprekṣya savrīḍam idam abravīt
english: Having drawn off the troops, Droṇa, exceedingly downcast, looked upon Duryodhana and spoke these words in shame.

sanskrit: uktam etan mayā pūrvaṃ na tiṣṭhati dhanaṃjaye śakyo grahītuṃ saṃgrāme devair api yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: "This I told you before: while Dhanaṃjaya holds his ground, Yudhiṣṭhira cannot be seized in battle, not even by the gods.

sanskrit: iti tad vaḥ prayatatāṃ kṛtaṃ pārthena saṃyuge mātiśaṅkīr vaco mahyam ajeyau kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau
english: So, though you strove, it was thwarted by Pārtha in the battle. Do not too greatly doubt my word: unconquerable are Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: apanīte tu yogena kena cic chvetavāhane tata eṣyati te rājan vaśam adya yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: But if by some device he of the white steeds be drawn away, then, O king, Yudhiṣṭhira shall this day come into your power.

sanskrit: kaś cid āhvayatāṃ saṃkhye deśam anyaṃ prakarṣatu tam ajitvā tu kaunteyo na nivartet kathaṃ cana
english: Let someone challenge him in the fight and draw him off to another quarter; for the son of Kuntī will in no wise return without having vanquished him."
